description:
FILED s470bn (Opus, 2026-09-05) from the round-27 ranked table
(docs/plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md Â§A.4.3).

THE MEASUREMENT.  sb-sprof, :cpu, 1 ms, thousands of samples per row:
  json-rt (N=400, 26 973 samples, 0 % compile):
    search 14.5 %  (graph: 23.7 % TOTAL, called from cl-ppcre's
                    `create-scanner-aux` scan closure â NOT from p-index)
    sb-kernel:vector-hairy-data-vector-ref/check-bounds 11.6 %
    the scanner closure itself 8.7 %
    (sb-vm::optimized-data-vector-ref character) 7.2 %
    char= 5.2 %, convert-char-class-to-test-function 4.5 %
  textproc (N=1 200, 12 202 samples, 0 % compile):
    hairy data-vector-ref 12.5 %, search 11.5 %, scanner closure 8.2 %,
    create-char-set-matcher closure 6.3 %, char= 4.5 %,
    pcl::do-regex-match 4.5 %, pcl::set-match-vars 3.6 %

THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, and it is cheap: a GENERIC `search` and a HAIRY
`data-vector-ref` inside a scan whose SUBJECT `do-regex-match` already coerced
to a simple-string (task #680) mean some OTHER operand is not simple.  Find it
before designing anything â print `(simple-string-p â¦)` for the subject, the
pattern and cl-ppcre's own literal-search argument at a hot site in each row.
If it is one `coerce`, this is an S lever worth a third of two rows.  If the
generic call is cl-ppcre's own type-agnostic code, the owner is A.2 row 11
(#71, the PCRE2 backend) and the number above is its price tag.

DO NOT re-derive: `do-regex-match` coerces the subject; `%p-regex-compiled`
caches the scanner, the reg-names, the closers and the modifier plist per op
(#680), so pattern TRANSLATION is not in these numbers (it was 26 % at N=60,
which is how a too-small N misreads this row).

=== DONE (s473q) === measured 2026-09-07; full record docs/pcre2-spike-s473q.md Â§7.

THE ANSWER: THERE IS NO NON-SIMPLE OPERAND TO COERCE.  Handing cl-ppcre the same
content as a simple-base-string and as a (simple-array character (*)) is worth
0.8%-1.3% - inside the control pair's noise - on BOTH the /g shape and the
literal-prefix shape (interleaved best-of-7, scratch/s473q/p1187.lisp).

THE CAUSE IS STATIC AND IT IS IN cl-ppcre, NOT PCL:
    ;; cl-ppcre/specials.lisp:71
    (declaim (simple-string *string*))
and SBCL's SIMPLE-STRING is the UNION (or (simple-array character (*))
(simple-array base-char (*)) (simple-array nil (*))), so every element access
inside cl-ppcre's compiled matchers is a runtime type dispatch NO MATTER WHAT
PCL HANDS IT.  That is the profile's hairy data-vector-ref, and the generic
`search` is cl-ppcre/scanner.lisp:72 calling SEARCH with a :test function on the
same union-typed special.

So THIS TASK'S OWN SECOND BRANCH FIRES: "If the generic call is cl-ppcre's own
type-agnostic code, the owner is A.2 row 11 (#71, the PCRE2 backend) and the
number above is its price tag."  The "S if it is one coercion" half is CLOSED,
unbuilt.  Ranked-table entries #2, #3, #5, #6, #8, #9 stay #71's.

BUT READING THAT SITE FOUND A DIFFERENT LEVER.  scanner.lisp:72 takes the
generic SEARCH only when cl-ppcre:*use-bmh-matchers* is NIL, which is its
DEFAULT (specials.lisp:126) and PCL has never bound it.  Binding it to T is
6.6x faster on a literal-prefix scan in isolation and reads textproc 0.743x
(+34.6%) at row level, ~0 elsewhere, for +8.8 MB of peak RSS - but the skip
table is *regex-char-code-limit* = 1,114,112 fixnums = 8.5 MB PER LITERAL
PATTERN and the limit cannot be lowered without breaking Unicode character
classes.  NOT SHIPPED HERE; filed with its numbers and its budget question as
#1461.
subject: CLOSED s473q by measurement: there is NO non-simple operand - cl-ppcre declaims *string* as the UNION type simple-string, so its accesses are generic whatever PCL hands it; the owner is #71.  A DIFFERENT lever found at the same site -> #1461
